olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find the least positive integer $N$ such that the digit sum of $N$ is 100 and the digit sum of $2N$ is 110.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Convex cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AC$ a diameter, center $O$. Parallelograms $DAOE$ and $BCOF$ are constructed. Show that if $E,F$ lie on the circumcircle, then $ABCD$ is a rectangle.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: 2008 bags numbered $1,\ldots,2008$, each with 2008 frogs. A move: choose a bag, remove some frogs (leaving $x\geq 0$); from each higher-numbered bag with more than $x$ frogs, frogs escape until $x$ remain. Player removing the last frog from bag 1 loses. Find a winning strategy.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Five girls share a store (Mon–Fri). Each works exactly 2 days per week; the 5 weekly pairs are all different. How many ways can the work schedule be arranged?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find a real-coefficient polynomial $p(x)$ satisfying $(x+10)p(2x)=(8x-32)p(x+6)$ for all real $x$ and $p(1)=210$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $P\in AB$, $Q\in AC$ so $BPQC$ is cyclic. Circumcircle of $\triangle ABQ$ meets $BC$ at $S$; circumcircle of $\triangle APC$ meets $BC$ at $R$. $PR\cap QS=L$. Prove $AL\cap BC$ is independent of the choice of $P,Q$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2008
